# std.heap

Binary heaps (round 5): `Heap<T>(by:)` pops the smallest key first and `Heap(by: desc)` the largest. One type per shape: `Heap`, `ErasableHeap`, `IndexedHeap`, `MeldHeap`, `MinMaxHeap`.  Ties: no heap here is stable. Among elements with equal keys under `by:`, which one `peek` shows and `pop` returns is unspecified (but `peek` always shows the one `pop` returns next). Without `by:`, equal elements are indistinguishable, so this never shows. For a fixed order among equals, put the tie-breaker in the entry: `(d, v)`, or `(d, desc(v))`.

In prelude (no `use` needed): `Heap`, `MaxHeap`, `MinHeap`, `Settle`.

## Types & Constants

- `type MinHeap<T> = Heap<T>` — `Heap<T>()`: pops the smallest first.

## `struct Heap<T>`

A priority queue on `<`.

Fields: `lt: ?((T, T) -> Bool)`.

- `fn new<K>(by: ?(T -> K) = None) -> Heap<T>` — \(O(1)\); Create an empty `Heap<T>`, optionally ordered by key extractor `by:` (W7).
- `fn of<K>(xs: List<T>, by: ?(T -> K) = None) -> Heap<T>` — \(O(n)\); Build a `Heap<T>` from `xs` via Floyd heapify.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); Number of elements currently in the heap.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether the heap is empty.
- `@get fn peek(self) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\); The smallest element, or `None` if the heap is empty.
- `fn clear(mut self)` — \(O(1)\); Remove all elements from the heap.
- `fn take(mut self) -> Heap<T>` — \(O(1)\); Move the heap's contents out in \(O(1)\), leaving `self` empty.
- `fn push(mut self, x: T)` — \(O(\log n)\), amortized over list growth; Push `x` into the heap.
- `fn pop(mut self) -> ?T` — \(O(\log n)\); Remove and return the smallest element, or `None` if the heap is empty.
- `fn reserve(mut self, cap: Int)` — \(O(\mathit{cap})\) when the storage grows, \(O(1)\) otherwise; Reserve backing storage for at least `cap` elements.
- `fn push_pop(mut self, x: T) -> T` — \(O(\log n)\); \(O(1)\) when `x` is returned; Push `x` and pop the minimum in one sift.
- `fn replace_top(mut self, x: T) -> ?T` — \(O(\log n)\); Replace the minimum with `x` and return the old minimum (or `None` if empty).
- `fn push_all(mut self, items: List<T>)` — \(O(k \log n)\) for `k` items; Push all elements of `items`.
- `fn drain(mut self) -> yields T` — \(O(\log n)\) per step; Pop and yield all elements in ascending order, leaving the heap empty.

## `struct ErasableHeap<T>`

Min-heap supporting \(O(\log n)\) arbitrary-value `remove(x)` via a lazy deletion heap.

Fields: `live: Heap<T>`, `dead: Heap<T>`.

- `fn new<K>(by: ?(T -> K) = None) -> ErasableHeap<T>` — \(O(1)\); Create an empty `ErasableHeap<T>`, optionally ordered by key extractor `by:` (W7).
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); Number of active elements in the heap.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether no active elements remain.
- `fn clear(mut self)` — \(O(1)\); Remove all elements from the heap.
- `fn take(mut self) -> ErasableHeap<T>` — \(O(1)\); Move the heap's contents out in \(O(1)\), leaving `self` empty.
- `fn push(mut self, x: T)` — \(O(\log n)\); Push `x` into the heap.
- `fn remove(mut self, x: T)` — \(O(\log n)\); Schedule one copy of `x` for lazy removal (`x` must be present).; traps: never in release; debug traps when `x` is found not to be present
- `fn peek(mut self) -> ?T` — \(O(\log n)\) amortized; Return the smallest active element, or `None` if empty.
- `fn pop(mut self) -> ?T` — \(O(\log n)\) amortized; Remove and return the smallest active element, or `None` if empty.

## `struct IndexedHeap<D, K>`

Domain-keyed min-heap over `D` supporting \(O(\log n)\) `set`, `decrease`, `increase`, `remove`, and `pop`, plus \(O(1)\) `contains`, `get`, and `peek`.

Fields: `heap: List<D>`, `pos: [D]Int`, `keys: [D]?K`.

- `fn new() -> IndexedHeap<D, K>` — \(O(\lvert D \rvert)\); Create an empty `IndexedHeap<D, K>`.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); Number of keys currently in the heap.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether the heap is empty.
- `fn contains(self, v: D) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether `v` is currently in the heap.
- `fn get(self, v: D) -> ?K` — \(O(1)\); Current priority of `v`, or `None` if absent.
- `@get fn peek(self) -> ?(D, K)` — \(O(1)\); Pair `(v, key)` with the smallest key, or `None` if empty.
- `fn clear(mut self)` — \(O(\mathit{len})\); Remove all entries from the heap.
- `fn set(mut self, v: D, k: K)` — \(O(\log n)\); Insert `v` with key `k`, or update `v`'s key to `k`.
- `fn decrease(mut self, v: D, k: K) -> Bool` — \(O(\log n)\); Insert `v` with `k`, or lower its key to `k` if `k` is smaller.
- `fn increase(mut self, v: D, k: K) -> Bool` — \(O(\log n)\); Insert `v` with `k`, or raise its key to `k` if `k` is larger.
- `fn remove(mut self, v: D) -> ?K` — \(O(\log n)\); Remove `v` from the heap if present; returns its old key or `None`.
- `fn pop(mut self) -> ?(D, K)` — \(O(\log n)\); Remove and return `(v, key)` with the smallest key, or `None` if empty.

## `struct MinMaxHeap<T>`

Fields: `lt: ?((T, T) -> Bool)`.

- `fn new<K>(by: ?(T -> K) = None) -> MinMaxHeap<T>` — \(O(1)\); Create an empty `MinMaxHeap<T>`, optionally ordered by key extractor `by:` (W7).
- `fn of(xs: List<T>) -> MinMaxHeap<T>` — \(O(n)\); Build a `MinMaxHeap<T>` from `xs` in linear time.
- `fn reserve(mut self, cap: Int)` — \(O(\mathit{cap})\) when the storage grows, \(O(1)\) otherwise; Reserve backing storage for at least `cap` elements.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); Number of elements currently in the heap.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether the heap is empty.
- `@get fn first(self) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\); The smallest element, or `None` if empty.
- `@get fn last(self) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\); The largest element, or `None` if empty.
- `fn push(mut self, x: T)` — \(O(\log n)\), amortized over list growth; Insert `x`.
- `fn pop_first(mut self) -> ?T` — \(O(\log n)\); Remove and return the smallest element, or `None` if empty.
- `fn pop_last(mut self) -> ?T` — \(O(\log n)\); Remove and return the largest element, or `None` if empty.
- `fn clear(mut self)` — \(O(1)\); Remove all elements.
- `fn take(mut self) -> MinMaxHeap<T>` — \(O(1)\); Move contents out in \(O(1)\), leaving `self` empty.

## `struct MeldHeap<T>`

Meldable min-heap (skew / leftist heap) with \(O(\log n)\) `meld` and, when `T: Add`, \(O(1)\) lazy offset `add_all`.

- `fn new<K>(by: ?(T -> K) = None) -> MeldHeap<T>` — \(O(1)\); Create an empty `MeldHeap<T>`, optionally ordered by key extractor `by:` (W7).
- `fn of(xs: List<T>) -> MeldHeap<T>` — \(O(n)\); Build a `MeldHeap<T>` from `xs`.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); Number of elements currently in the heap.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether the heap is empty.
- `@get fn peek(self) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\); The smallest element, or `None` if empty.
- `@get fn top(self) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\); The smallest element, or `None` if empty (alias for `peek`).
- `fn push(mut self, x: T)` — \(O(\log n)\); Push `x` into the heap.
- `fn push_all(mut self, items: List<T>)` — \(O(k \log n)\) for `k` items; Push all elements of `items`.
- `fn pop(mut self) -> ?T` — \(O(\log n)\); Remove and return the smallest element, or `None` if empty.
- `fn meld(mut self, other: MeldHeap<T>)` — \(O(\log n)\); Meld `other` into `self` (consuming `other`).
- `fn absorb(mut self, mut other: MeldHeap<T>)` — \(O(\log n)\); Meld `other` into `self`, leaving `other` empty.
- `fn add_all(mut self, delta: T) where T: Add` — \(O(1)\); Add `delta` lazily to every element (for additive types).; traps: never (overflow wraps in release, traps in debug)
- `fn clear(mut self)` — \(O(1)\); Remove all elements.
- `fn take(mut self) -> MeldHeap<T>` — \(O(1)\); Move contents out in \(O(1)\), leaving `self` empty.
- `fn drain(mut self) -> List<T>` — \(O(n \log n)\); Pop and return all elements in ascending order, leaving `self` empty.

## `struct MaxHeap<T>`

`Heap<T>(by: desc)` under its own name: pops the largest first, with the same operations and costs as `Heap`; it holds each element as `desc(x)`.

Fields: `h: Heap<Desc<T>>`.

- `fn new() -> MaxHeap<T>` — \(O(1)\); An empty `MaxHeap<T>`.
- `fn of(xs: List<T>) -> MaxHeap<T>` — \(O(n)\); Build a `MaxHeap<T>` from `xs` via Floyd heapify.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); Number of elements currently in the heap.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether the heap is empty.
- `@get fn peek(self) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\); The largest element, or `None` when empty.
- `fn clear(mut self)` — \(O(1)\); Remove every element.
- `fn take(mut self) -> MaxHeap<T>` — \(O(1)\); Move the contents out, leaving this heap empty.
- `fn push(mut self, x: T)` — \(O(\log n)\); Add `x`.
- `fn pop(mut self) -> ?T` — \(O(\log n)\); Remove and return the largest element, or `None` when empty.
- `fn reserve(mut self, cap: Int)` — \(O(\mathit{cap})\) when the storage grows, \(O(1)\) otherwise; Make room for `cap` elements in total.
- `fn push_pop(mut self, x: T) -> T` — \(O(\log n)\); \(O(1)\) when `x` is returned; Push `x`, then pop and return the largest element.
- `fn replace_top(mut self, x: T) -> ?T` — \(O(\log n)\); Pop the largest element, then push `x`; returns the popped one, or `None` (and only pushes) when empty.
- `fn push_all(mut self, items: List<T>)` — \(O(n + k \log(n + k))\); Push every element of `items`.
- `fn drain(mut self) -> yields T` — \(O(n \log n)\); Pop every element, largest first.

## `struct Settle<K, P>(best: (P, P) -> P = min)`

A keyed frontier where each key pops exactly once.

- `fn offer(mut self, k: K, p: P)` — \(O(\log n)\) amortized, `n` the offers so far; Offer priority `p` for key `k`: an unsettled key keeps `best(old, p)` (or `p` when it had None); a settled key ignores the offer.
- `fn pop(mut self) -> ?(K, P)` — \(O(\log n)\) amortized, `n` the offers so far; Settle and return the unsettled key whose priority is best, with that priority, or `None` when every offered key has settled.
- `fn settled(self, k: K) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\) expected; Whether `k` has popped.
- `fn get(self, k: K) -> ?P` — \(O(1)\) expected; The best priority offered for `k` so far (for a settled key, the one it popped with), or `None` if `k` was never offered.

## Example

```cp
var h = MinHeap<Int>()
h.push(7)
h.push(2)
h.push(5)
print(h.pop()!, h.pop()!)
// output: 2 5
```
